legibility: The scan exposes most thin strokes clearly, but this hand frequently compresses short vowels and joins several letters into low horizontal traces. The generator relation and following looped glyph remain ambiguous; cancellation masks the earlier wording at two upper loci. The raised correction at associant exposes strokes but not the old letter value. Barycentres has heavy low retracing whose deletion status remains open. The tiny points below the writing level after cas have no syntactic attachment and are excluded as incidental marks; the entire line remains in the blind reading box list. notes:
On manuscript page 4, lines 1–8 state that Z/6Z acts transitively on the written nonzero 2-torsion set, with ±1 acting trivially, and call the set a torsor under the written quotient ≃ Z/3Z. The generator annotation remains doubtful and the exponential is transcribed exactly as 2π/6 without i. The passage identifies the torsor with S/±1 through the midpoint of each written radius and its image in X_S; the raised closing curve has no settled attachment. Lines 9–17 state that the fixed-point set for the written subgroup has cardinal 3, describe barycentres of six triangles in the central subdivision, give the barred example, and group these into two packets of three congruent under the written Γ, yielding two symmetric elements of order 3. These are accounts of the source’s statements, with its uncertainties preserved. The first reader performed no proof check or computation. The root check follows.

Root check 148_scan011-CHECK-hexagonal-torsion, for the base C/Z[zeta] explicitly written on 148_scan009. In the basis (1,zeta), the displayed relation zeta^2+zeta+1=0 gives multiplication by zeta as M(a,b)=(-b,a-b). The source minus-conjugate generator has matrix J=I+M, since conjugation sends zeta to zeta^2=-1-zeta. Direct integer multiplication gives J^3=-I and J^6=I. Modulo 2, J cycles the three nonzero numerator pairs (1,0), (1,1), (0,1). For fixed points of M, the exact identity (M-I)(M+2I)=-3I puts every fixed torus class in the group killed by 3. Enumerating its nine numerator pairs modulo 3 leaves exactly (0,0), (2,1) and (1,2). The last two have order 3. The written (1-bar(zeta))/3 has numerator (2,1); H's unbarred candidate has numerator (1,2). Their sum is a lattice vector, so they are the two opposite nonzero fixed classes. This computation therefore leaves the bar decision to the ink, where a separate overbar is visible. The source exponential is retained exactly as exp(2 pi/6), with no i supplied. Certificate: work/hexagonal_torsion_check.json; script: scripts/check_hexagonal_torsion.py. These checks concern the displayed base lattice and the named finite actions; no further assertion about arbitrary torsors is made.

After inspecting the existing example crop, root omitted the two tiny low points following cas: their level and size, and the absence of a punctuation attachment within cas épinglé, do not support a source colon. No mark is supplied at that place; the complete line is included in the blind second-reading box list.

Before the blind second reading, root compared the compressed terminal formation with the analogous word on scan 013 and withdrew the resolution of M0105. The full reading mutuellement remains first, with the contracted mutuellem and raised t retained as an alternative; the local low strokes do not independently separate the complete ending. This is a certainty revision, with no added lexical error count.
Blind audit: the low runs and raised terminal strokes favor contracted transitivem with raised t and mutuellem with raised t; the full-word alternatives remain. The lower cancellation and raised determiner before torseur retain narrower local alternatives. The broad barred zeta in the two formulas was compared with the scan 009 definition and labels; the narrow j|zeta glyph and the source fraction without i remain unchanged.
